<!-- en -->
v0.1.9 is a deliberate breaking release: the command surface is consolidated into two explicit service groups — `token-usage daemon start|status|stop|restart` manages the collection daemon and `token-usage serve start|status|stop|restart` manages the local dashboard — the six analysis commands and the top-level lifecycle commands are removed, the dashboard no longer runs in the foreground, `doctor`, `daemon status`, and `serve status` gain machine-readable JSON output, and a self-update now preserves a running dashboard just as it preserves a running daemon.

### Breaking changes
- The six analysis commands `chart`, `compare`, `export`, `forecast`, `report`, and `top` are removed without compatibility aliases. The visual analytics — SVG charts, usage forecasts, period comparisons, and top-session rankings — live on in the `serve` dashboard over its read-only HTTP data surface, including page-scoped CSV export there; terminal reports remain `query` and `watch`. The machine-readable CLI export contract and the offline HTML report bundle were removed intentionally and have no full replacement.
- The top-level lifecycle commands are gone: `token-usage start` / `status` / `stop` / `restart` are now `token-usage daemon start` / `daemon status` / `daemon stop` / `daemon restart`. The semantics are unchanged — nginx-style idempotent start and stop, the autostart definition stays decoupled from the running process, and restart still stops the old daemon and starts a new one under a single process-control lock.
- Bare `token-usage serve` no longer runs a foreground server: `serve` is a pure command group whose bare form only prints help (an unknown subcommand fails with `unknown command`), and the dashboard always runs in the background via `serve start` / `serve restart`, inspected and stopped by `serve status` / `serve stop`. The `--addr` and `--open` flags are unchanged (`--open` now launches the browser after the background server is confirmed up). The single-instance contract, state-file lifecycle, and probe-verified stop are unchanged.

### Highlights
- The `daemon` command group is the new home of the collection daemon's lifecycle. `daemon start` runs the daemon in the background (nginx-style, idempotent when already running), `daemon status` reports the runtime state and the autostart drift check, `daemon stop` is idempotent and never touches the autostart definition, and `daemon restart` swaps processes under one control lock. The daemon and the dashboard are separate services: their PIDs, locks, state files, logs, and ports do not overlap, and stopping or restarting one never affects the other.
- `token-usage update` now preserves the local dashboard's running state exactly as it preserves the daemon's: a dashboard that answers on `/api/meta` before the update is stopped for the replacement — on Windows this also releases the old `.exe` so the background helper can complete it — and then restored as a background instance at its original address with the new binary; a stopped dashboard is not started, and the automatic restore never opens a browser. Only an answering dashboard counts as running (a missing, corrupt, or stale `serve.json` is treated as not running and left untouched); if the dashboard cannot be stopped, the update aborts with the binary unreplaced; if any later step fails, the update rolls back to the old binary and the pre-update daemon/dashboard state, keeping the primary and the rollback failure messages. Before stopping anything, the update persists a recovery snapshot of both services' running state — alongside it, the POSIX transaction journal and the Windows helper plan record the same state with the replacement transaction — so an interrupted update restores the services on the next run, whether the process was killed after the services were stopped but before the replacement began, or on Windows after the replacement had landed but before the services were brought back, and the lifecycle actions reuse the same internal orchestration as `serve stop` / `serve start` (no CLI subprocess, no shell).
- `doctor` gains a Dashboard check. It reads `serve.json` and probes the recorded `/api/meta`: a running instance is reported OK with its URL and PID, a stale or corrupt state file is a WARN pointing at `token-usage serve status` for cleanup, an absent state file is an informational line, and a config failure skips the check. The probe is read-only by construction — no state-lock acquisition, no state-file removal, and no request at all when `serve.json` is absent.
- `doctor --format json` emits the full health report as machine-readable JSON: `checks` is an array of `{id, label, status, detail}` with stable ids (`config`, `data_directory`, `database`, `clients`, `last_collection`, `data_freshness`, `date_consistency`, `unresolved_errors`, `query_definitions`, `daemon`, `dashboard`) and `status` in a closed set (`ok`/`warn`/`fail`/`skipped`/`info`, same semantics as the table words); `summary` carries `result` (`ok`/`warn`/`fail`, FAIL over WARN), `warnings`, and `problems`. The table output is unchanged apart from the daemon line's command pointer, which now reads `token-usage daemon status`.
- `daemon status --format json` emits the same snapshot the table shows as a machine-readable document: `running` and `pid` from the daemon lock, `startup_phase` (`null` when not running; `available`, `monitor_ready`, `catch_up`, `catch_up_failures` — unavailable phase metadata and unknown catch-up values degrade to `unknown`), `data_dir`, `poll_interval_seconds`, and `autostart` (`configured`, `definition_exists`, `spec_matches`, boolean `detect_failed` with `detect_error` (present when detection fails), and `status` in a closed set: `enabled`/`missing`/`drift`/`residual`/`disabled`, or `unknown`). Together with `errors --format json`, scripts and AI agents can poll and diagnose without parsing terminal tables.
- `serve status --format json` emits the same outcome as the table as a machine-readable document, completing the JSON trio with `doctor --format json` and `daemon status --format json`: `state` uses a closed vocabulary (`running`, `not_running`, `not_running_stale_removed`, `not_running_corrupt_removed`), `running` is the boolean the state derives from, `pid`, `addr`, `url`, and `started_at` (RFC3339, verbatim from serve.json) appear only while running, and `data_dir` carries the configured data directory. The output is two-space indented with a trailing newline; the table output is unchanged.

### Fixed
- The installer's running-daemon detection uses `token-usage daemon status` (previously the bare `status` form, which would silently never match after the command-surface consolidation) and its guidance points at `token-usage daemon restart`; the Windows installer's file-lock message and post-install hints use `daemon stop` / `daemon start` forms.
- The migration guidance in the README and the CLI reference no longer implies that the removed `export`/`report` commands are fully replaceable: the dashboard's export is page-scoped, the machine-readable CLI export contract and the offline report bundle are gone intentionally, and terminal querying is `query`/`watch`.
- Internal comments, help text, and user-facing guidance and error messages no longer refer to a foreground `serve` execution path that no longer exists or to the removed bare lifecycle commands (update completion hints, config-save step suggestions, and the daemon-restart error among them); the architecture document's dependency graph now matches the actual package imports after the consolidation.

### Installation
See the [README Quick Start](https://github.com/YuLaiZ/token-usage#quick-start). Existing users update in place with `token-usage update` — after upgrading, start the daemon with `token-usage daemon start` and the dashboard with `token-usage serve start`; the removed commands fail with `unknown command`, and the migration table in the README (and the CLI reference) lists the available migration paths along with the boundaries of what was removed.

<!-- zh -->
v0.1.9 是一次有意的破坏性版本：命令面收敛为两个显式服务组——`token-usage daemon start|status|stop|restart` 管理采集守护进程、`token-usage serve start|status|stop|restart` 管理本地仪表板——六个分析命令与顶层生命周期命令被移除，仪表板不再前台运行，`doctor`、`daemon status` 与 `serve status` 新增机器可读的 JSON 输出，且自更新现在会像保持运行中的 daemon 一样保持运行中的仪表板。

### 破坏性变更
- 六个分析命令 `chart`、`compare`、`export`、`forecast`、`report`、`top` 被移除，无兼容别名。可视化分析——SVG 图表、用量预测、两期对比、最重会话排行——由 `serve` 仪表板经只读 HTTP 数据面延续，含页面范围内的 CSV 导出；终端查询继续由 `query` 与 `watch` 承担。机器可读的 CLI export 合同与离线 HTML 报告包已有意移除，没有完整直接替代。
- 顶层生命周期命令移除：`token-usage start` / `status` / `stop` / `restart` 变为 `token-usage daemon start` / `daemon status` / `daemon stop` / `daemon restart`。语义不变——nginx 风格的幂等启动与停止、自启定义与运行进程解耦、restart 仍在单把进程控制锁内停旧起新。
- 裸 `token-usage serve` 不再前台运行：`serve` 是纯命令组，裸执行只打印帮助（未知子命令报 `unknown command`），仪表板始终经 `serve start` / `serve restart` 后台运行，由 `serve status` / `serve stop` 查看与停止。`--addr` 与 `--open` 标志不变（`--open` 现在在后台服务确认就绪后打开浏览器）。单实例契约、状态文件生命周期与探活判停均不变。

### 亮点
- `daemon` 命令组成为采集守护进程生命周期的新家。`daemon start` 后台启动守护进程（nginx 风格，已运行时幂等），`daemon status` 报告运行态与自启漂移检测，`daemon stop` 幂等且绝不触碰自启定义，`daemon restart` 在单把控制锁内换进程。守护进程与仪表板是两个独立服务：PID、锁、状态文件、日志与端口互不重叠，停止或重启其中一个绝不影响另一个。
- `token-usage update` 现在像保持 daemon 一样保持本地仪表板的运行态：更新前对 `/api/meta` 有应答的 dashboard 会被停止以完成替换——Windows 上这一步同时释放旧 `.exe` 供后台 helper 完成——随后以原监听地址、用新二进制后台恢复；原本停止的 dashboard 不会被启动，自动恢复绝不打开浏览器。只有有应答的 dashboard 才算在运行（缺失、损坏或陈旧的 `serve.json` 一律按未运行处理且不被改动）；dashboard 无法停止时更新中止、二进制保持原样；其后任一步失败时更新回滚到旧二进制与更新前的 daemon/dashboard 运行态，并同时保留主失败与回滚失败信息。在停止任何服务之前，更新会先持久化两个服务运行态的恢复快照（POSIX 事务 journal 与 Windows helper plan 随替换事务一并记录同一状态），因此中断的更新会在下一次运行时还原服务——无论是进程在服务已停止、替换尚未开始之后被杀，还是 Windows 上替换已落地、服务尚未恢复时被杀；生命周期动作与 `serve stop` / `serve start` 复用同一套内部编排（不经 CLI 子进程、不经 shell）。
- `doctor` 新增仪表板检查。读取 `serve.json` 并探活记录的 `/api/meta`：运行中的实例报 OK（含 URL 与 PID），陈旧或损坏的状态文件报 WARN 并指向 `token-usage serve status` 清理，状态文件缺失为提示行，配置失败时跳过该项。探测按构造只读——不取状态锁、不删除状态文件，`serve.json` 不存在时不发任何请求。
- `doctor --format json` 把完整健康报告输出为机器可读 JSON：`checks` 是 `{id, label, status, detail}` 数组，id 稳定（`config`、`data_directory`、`database`、`clients`、`last_collection`、`data_freshness`、`date_consistency`、`unresolved_errors`、`query_definitions`、`daemon`、`dashboard`），status 取封闭值域（`ok`/`warn`/`fail`/`skipped`/`info`，与 table 状态词语义一致）；`summary` 携带 `result`（`ok`/`warn`/`fail`，FAIL 优先于 WARN）、`warnings` 与 `problems`。table 输出不变，仅 Daemon 行的命令指引更新为 `token-usage daemon status`。
- `daemon status --format json` 把 table 所示同一快照输出为机器可读文档：来自 daemon lock 的 `running` 与 `pid`、`startup_phase`（未运行时为 `null`；含 `available`、`monitor_ready`、`catch_up`、`catch_up_failures`——阶段元数据不可得与未知补采值都降级为 `unknown`）、`data_dir`、`poll_interval_seconds`，以及 `autostart`（`configured`、`definition_exists`、`spec_matches`、布尔 `detect_failed` 与条件出现的 `detect_error`（检测失败时携带原因），`status` 取封闭值域：`enabled`/`missing`/`drift`/`residual`/`disabled`，检测不可行时为 `unknown`）。加上既有的 `errors --format json`，脚本与 AI agent 可以不解析终端表格即可轮询与诊断。
- `serve status --format json` 把 table 的同一判定输出为机器可读文档，与 `doctor --format json`、`daemon status --format json` 组成完整的三件套：`state` 取封闭值域（`running`、`not_running`、`not_running_stale_removed`、`not_running_corrupt_removed`），`running` 是 state 对应的布尔值，`pid`、`addr`、`url` 与 `started_at`（RFC3339，serve.json 原值）仅在运行中出现，`data_dir` 为配置的数据目录。输出为两空格缩进 + 尾随换行；table 输出不变。

### 修复
- 安装脚本的运行中守护进程探测改用 `token-usage daemon status`（此前为裸 `status` 形态，命令面收敛后将静默失配）并提示 `token-usage daemon restart`；Windows 安装器的文件占用报错与安装后提示改用 `daemon stop` / `daemon start` 形态。
- README 与 CLI 参考中的迁移指引不再暗示被删除的 `export`/`report` 可被完整替代：仪表板的导出是页面范围的，机器可读 CLI export 合同与离线报告包已有意移除，终端查询是 `query`/`watch`。
- 内部注释、帮助文本与用户可见的指引和错误消息不再引用已不存在的前台 `serve` 执行路径或已移除的裸生命周期命令（含 update 完成提示、config 保存后的步骤建议与 daemon restart 错误消息）；架构文档的依赖图已与收敛后的实际包导入对齐。

### 安装
见 [README 快速开始](https://github.com/YuLaiZ/token-usage/blob/main/README.zh-CN.md#快速开始)。已有用户用 `token-usage update` 原地升级——升级后用 `token-usage daemon start` 启动守护进程、`token-usage serve start` 启动仪表板；被移除的命令会报 `unknown command`，README（及 CLI 参考）中的迁移表列出可用的迁移路径与已移除能力的边界。
